title: Oh God, That Mad'st the Earth and Sky
description: Oh God, That Mad'st the Earth and Sky in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Reginald Heber wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 545, “In the Day of Distress”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Oh God, that mad'st the earth and sky, The dark-ness and the day, Oh lis-ten to Thy chil-dren's cry, And help us when we pray!

lines: Oh God, that mad'st the earth and sky,
Oh listen to Thy children's cry,
And help us when we pray!
For wide the waves of bitterness
And heavy grows the burdened heart,
The cross our Master bore for us,
For him we fain would bear;
But mortal strength to weakness turns,
Have mercy on our failings, Lord!
And when his sorrows visit us,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Reginald Heber died in 1826.
credits: Words by Reginald Heber (1783–1826), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
